event.piper_heart2.1.text: Thumb there, two fingers, now pull. ...Your hands are shaking. That's fine. Shaking is just vibrato. Keep going.
event.piper_heart2.1.why: frightened: she reads the player's state and turns it into a kind musical joke

event.piper_heart2.1.text: Thumb there, two fingers there, now pull. ...There. You're a musician now. You look tired, though. Long night?
event.piper_heart2.1.why: uneasy: an ordinary friend noticing the player is worn

event.piper_heart2.2.text: Here, a sunflower for your first gig. Cheapest sun there is. Come back Friday, early, while it's still light.
event.piper_heart2.2.why: frightened: the cheerful sign-off becomes a kind 'come while it's light'

event.piper_heart5.2.text: It usually ends on four old notes. ...Not tonight. You look like you need a happier ending. I'll find one.
event.piper_heart5.2.why: frightened: she drops the strange ending for the player's sake without knowing why it matters

event.piper_heart5.2.text: It ends on four notes. Old Mr. Fenn hummed them at the bar. Nobody taught me. I just woke up knowing them.
event.piper_heart5.2.why: clue: ties the notes to Edmund; unaware, no explanation

event.piper_heart5.2.text: It ends on four notes I hum when nobody's around. Lately somebody finishes them for me. I keep meaning to find out who.
event.piper_heart5.2.why: uneasy full: the hum answered, echoing the thread without repeating it

event.piper_heart5.2.text: It ends on four notes I hum when nobody's around. They stick like burrs. I keep meaning to find out where they're from.
event.piper_heart5.2.why: uneasy mild: the notes as a small itch

event.hall_dance.4.text: Same song, bigger room. Stay up front, [player]. It's warmer by the stage, and I play better with you close.
event.hall_dance.4.why: frightened: practical warmth, keeps the player near

event.hall_dance.4.text: Same song, bigger room. One verse, then I step off. Somebody's humming already, and I haven't started. Nice!
event.hall_dance.4.why: uneasy: the room is ahead of her; she takes it as a compliment

dlg.story.umbrella.talk.1.text: Third time it's wandered off. It always turns up drier than me, handle pointed at the woods. What do we do?
dlg.story.umbrella.talk.1.why: uneasy full: a small wrongness, played as umbrella comedy

dlg.story.umbrella.talk.r1.text: Leave it? ...Yes. A little red landmark. Anyone out late needs something bright to walk toward.
dlg.story.umbrella.talk.r1.why: frightened: the landmark becomes a light to walk home by

event.story_band_battle.intro.text: Two bands, one square, one very polite war. Judge quickly, [player]. Folks are heading in early tonight. Honest means fiddle.
event.story_band_battle.intro.why: uneasy: the square emptying early, noticed and shrugged off

dlg.story.band.talk.0.text: Exhibit A: one fiddle, one voice, and every lamp I could borrow. Stand by the light. Try not to swoon.
dlg.story.band.talk.0.why: frightened: she has quietly made the square brighter

event.piper_heart4.intro.text: Last set, and the room's half empty. You pick. Something bright, maybe? I'll play it like I wrote it.
event.piper_heart4.intro.why: frightened: nudges toward cheer for the player

event.piper_heart4.intro.text: Last set, and everyone's gone home early again. You pick. Anything. I'll play it like I wrote it.

dlg.piper.request.r0.text: A ballad. Sad in the middle, happy at the end. I'll lean hard on the happy end tonight. Gather round.

event.piper_heart6.intro.text: Down here. The cellar. ...You look worse than I feel, and I'm hiding among barrels. Sit. They're very supportive.
event.piper_heart6.intro.why: frightened: her stage fright yields to concern for the player

event.piper_heart6.intro.text: Down here. The cellar. It's so quiet down here, and I hate quiet. The barrels are supportive, though.
event.piper_heart6.intro.why: uneasy: her fear of silence given a little weight

dlg.piper.fright.r1.text: ...You didn't fill it. The quiet's been heavy lately. Not with you here. It's not so bad, shared.
dlg.piper.fright.r1.why: uneasy full: the village silence is felt, shared, survived

event.piper_heart6.after.text: The nerves fit in the fiddle case now. Those four old notes don't. They hum along down here. Tonight, I'll go up anyway.
event.piper_heart6.after.why: clue: the notes follow her into the cellar; unexplained

dlg.piper.chorus.0.text: The verse is about someone arriving at an old farm. The chorus is about where they end up. What is it?
dlg.piper.chorus.0.why: uneasy full: the song leans toward Edmund's farm and its open ending

dlg.piper.chorus.r0.text: Home. ...Oh. That's it. A word to hold on to. You look like you could use one tonight.
dlg.piper.chorus.r0.why: frightened: same choice, offered back as comfort

event.piper_heart10.intro.text: Tonight we play the song we wrote. Stay where I can see you. After the first verse, I step off.
event.piper_heart10.intro.why: frightened: she keeps the player in sight

event.piper_heart10.intro.text: Tonight we play our song. I start it, then step off. If the room hums something else underneath, just keep singing.
event.piper_heart10.intro.why: uneasy full: the four notes under the chorus, unnamed

event.piper_friend.doing.text: 'Oh parsnip, pale and patient root...' You're not laughing. That's okay. It rhymes with 'boot'. I'll keep going.
event.piper_friend.doing.why: frightened: the joke falls flat and she stays kind

event.piper_friend.wrap.text: That's a chorus! A bad one. Mine. Get some sleep, then come back Friday. Verse five is about you.
event.piper_friend.wrap.why: uneasy: an ordinary friend's 'get some sleep'

event.piper_birthday.intro.text: My birthday! I wrote myself a song. You look worn out, so take the good seat. It's a modest masterpiece.
event.piper_birthday.intro.why: uneasy: gives the player the good seat

event.piper_courtship.intro.text: So. A love song and a coward's song. You've had a long week, so here's the coward's. Would you court me? It scans if you say yes.
event.piper_courtship.intro.why: frightened: softer, aware of the player's state

event.piper_courtship2.intro.text: Me again. The coward's song has a second verse now. You look tired, so I'll keep it short. Still scans if you say yes.

dlg.piper.partners.r2.text: A walk home after. I'll hum, you hum. Just not those four old notes. Out there, the dark joins in.
dlg.piper.partners.r2.why: clue: the notes answered at night, outdoors

dlg.piper.partners.r2.text: A walk home after. The nights are too quiet lately. Good thing I'm loud. I'll hum the whole way.
dlg.piper.partners.r2.why: uneasy: she fills the quiet on purpose

event.overheard_wren_piper_1.l2.text: I'm not flat, the stool's tilted! Or the room is. Everything leans funny lately!
event.overheard_wren_piper_1.l2.why: uneasy full: shadows lean wrong, as stool comedy

event.overheard_wren_piper_2.l4.text: It's perfect. I'm stealing it. ...Wren, why'd you go pale on 'awake'?
event.overheard_wren_piper_2.l4.why: hint: a Keeper flinches at her own word; Piper only notices

event.overheard_wren_piper_3.l4.text: Pencil it is. Closing early tonight? You always do, this night of the season.
event.overheard_wren_piper_3.l4.why: hint: the saloon closes early on the same night each season

event.overheard_wren_piper_4.l4.text: Deal! Make it a duet. And Wren? Sleep. You look like you've been up all month.
event.overheard_wren_piper_4.l4.why: uneasy full: a Keeper's tiredness, seen by a friend

event.overheard_piper_juno_1.l3.text: I felt it in my teeth! ...You stopped. So why is something still humming?
event.overheard_piper_juno_1.l3.why: uneasy full: the low hum, under the forge joke

event.overheard_piper_juno_2.l3.text: One, two, clang! That's a chorus! ...Juno, is your fire meant to go blue?
event.overheard_piper_juno_2.l3.why: uneasy full: the forge fire burns blue-ish, noticed not explained

event.overheard_piper_juno_3.l3.text: Then it gets my best set! Front row's yours, Juno. Face it toward the square.
event.overheard_piper_juno_3.l3.why: uneasy: she turns the stage away from the woods without saying why

event.overheard_hazel_piper_1.l3.text: It was you! 'Moon' rhymes with 'soon' now. You circled every new moon too. Why?
event.overheard_hazel_piper_1.l3.why: hint: Hazel's date-counting leaks into the songbook

event.overheard_hazel_piper_2.l3.text: ...Oh! That's it! Hazel, you look tired. Is the library keeping you up?
event.overheard_hazel_piper_2.l3.why: uneasy: Hazel's own fear, seen as tiredness

event.overheard_hazel_piper_3.l3.text: That's where it came from? It ends on my four notes. I never told you those.
event.overheard_hazel_piper_3.l3.why: clue: Hazel knows the notes; Piper is puzzled, not suspicious

adds.text: Quiet in here tonight. New moon soon, and the room always thins out. More stool for us!
adds.why: hint: the saloon empties around the new moon

adds.text: ...Did you hear that? The last note. Somebody finished it for me.
adds.why: uneasy full: the hum answered, in the room, for the player to hear

adds.text: ...They're humming four old notes under it. All of them. I never wrote those in.
adds.why: clue: the whole village knows Edmund's notes; Piper does not know why

adds.text: Last time it was hooked on the forest gate. Gate shut tight, umbrella wide open. Somebody's got a sense of humor.
adds.why: hint: points at the gate that stays shut

adds.text: Funny. Tilda, Marcus and the doctor slipped off before the last tune. Same night every season.
adds.why: hint: a pattern of Keepers leaving early, noticed and left unexplained

cuts.why: the 'I'm completely fine' joke is too brittle next to a shaken player
the clap-anyway bit falls flat when the player is frightened; the scene goes straight to the ending

notes: event.hall_dance.5 and every '.after'/'.outro' line built on {if choice:...} chains are left without variants: a variant cannot carry the choice branches without {if} markup.
Existing thread mythos.thread.piper.notes says 'the room hums them back'; variants echo it ('somebody finishes them', 'the dark joins in') without repeating it.
Piper names 'Old Mr. Fenn' only at the clue tier (lore>=3, hearts>=4), as a man who hummed at the bar, nothing more.
